in_hebrew.name: נורברט
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נורברט הוא שם פרטי ממקור גרמני, נגזר מ-nord ו-brecht, שפירושו 'אור צפוני' או 'תאורה מצפון'. השם נוצר בשילוב של שני היסודות, 'נורד' שפירושו צפון ו-'ברכט' שפירושו בהיר או זורח. השם נמצא בשימוש נרחב בקרב הנוצרים והוא קשור לסנט נורברט, קדוש נוצרי בן המאה ה-12.

in_greek.name: Νορβέρτος
in_greek.meaning: Νορβέρτος - βόρειος φως, φως από τον βορρά
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Νορβέρτος είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από τη γερμανική γλώσσα και συγκεκριμένα από τις λέξεις 'nord' που σημαίνει βορράς και 'brecht' που σημαίνει φωτεινός ή λάμψης. Το όνομα αυτό συνδέεται με τον Άγιο Νορβέρτο, έναν Χριστιανό άγιο του 12ου αιώνα, που ήταν γνωστός για την πνευματική του καθοδήγηση και τη συμβολή του στην Εκκλησία.

in_latin.name: Norbertus
in_latin.meaning: Northern brightness, shining from the north
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Norbertus is derived from the Germanic words 'nord' meaning north and 'brecht' meaning bright or shining. This name was popularized by Saint Norbert, a 12th-century Christian saint and founder of the Premonstratensian order, known for his spiritual leadership and ecclesiastical reforms.

in_english.long_meaning: The name Norbert originates from the Germanic languages, specifically from 'nord' meaning 'north' and 'bert' meaning 'bright' or 'famous'. It is associated with Saint Norbert of Xanten, a 12th-century Christian saint and reformer who founded the Premonstratensian order. The name symbolizes illumination and spiritual guidance from the north, reflecting the saint's influential role in Christian history.

saint_reference.note: Founder of the Premonstratensian order, known for his spiritual reforms and contributions to the Christian Church in the 12th century.

data.cultural_impact: Norbert of Xanten was a German Benedictine monk who is recognized as a reformer of the Benedictine order. He founded the Premonstratensian Order (Order of Canons Regular of Prémontré), also known as the Norbertines, in the early 12th century. The order, which was around 7,500 strong at the height of its expansion, was a semi-monastic institution that combined regular canons, secular priests, and lay brothers, emphasizing both prayer and action. This new order attracted many young men through its commitment to both study and practical work. The foundation of the Norbertines had a significant impact on Christian communities by offering an alternative monastic life style that allowed for a more balanced between contemplative prayer and active service.
data.spiritual_significance: St. Norbert is considered a patron saint of various causes, including orators, fishermen, and college students. He is also known for his emphasis on penance and his significant role in the revival of the Benedictine Order. Norbertine spirituality emphasizes the importance of living a simple and penitential life, seeking to develop the inner spiritual life through a disciplined exterior life. St. Norbert believed that through the imitation of Christ and the example of the saints, one could grow closer to God and deepen one's faith. His life and teachings serve as a powerful reminder that by living a dedicated Christian life, one can bring about positive change in the world and draw closer to the divine.
